items.title: Carolyn Buck Interview, 1969-03-25
items.q: he was so proud when I entered him into the school with David and Graham, his grandchildren.

ctx.x: Did George ever talk about integration and color children?

Yes. We spoke with him quite a bit. George is a very honest person, and he was very honest and open with me especially. Naturally, both being different colors. We both knew the burden we had to face with the population and so forth. And he naturally was all for integration. He was schooled in an integrated school his early years. He couldn't understand the riots that are going on now. He says that the people were bringing it upon themselves, both races. Not one, but the other, both races. He was very frank with…

He was a very honest, forthright person. If he liked the person, he couldn't do enough for him. If he didn't, he would either keep clear out of the way or you would know it, one way or another. He wasn't one to, like they say, pussyfoot around. He used to hurt him so many times going to the clubs and he'd have to walk in the back way. Because I know many times after I arrived, if he played in one or two hotels or something, he said it wasn't long before this, he said I'd have to go in the back way. He said, well…
